_comments: Declares Contracts -> Contract Template Modifications as a related-record collection (MJ 6.1).
This row is the whole of D-15 in the data model. CodeGen reads RelatedRecordCollection and emits
a typed `Modifications` accessor onto the GENERATED entity class, so browser and server both get
it: the modifications editor adds rows in the browser and ONE contract.Save() writes header and
rows in one transaction (plan §6.3). That is what let the rebuild delete the Contracts.SaveContract
remote operation, ContractDraft (688 lines) and the client-side hydrator — machinery whose entire
job was carrying child rows over the wire.
NO Sequence policy. A modification has no positional column: it is identified by WHICH PROVISION
it names, not by where it sits in a list. Declaring a sequence against a field that does not exist
fails at save time. Same shape as orders' Payment Lines, and for the same reason.
OrderBy __mj_CreatedAt ASC — capture order. There is no meaningful business ordering (provision
number would be plausible, but it lives on the joined provision row, not here), so the honest
answer is the order finance recorded them in. The editor groups by provision on screen anyway.
OnRemove 'delete': true composition. A modification without its contract means nothing — it is a
sentence about a clause with no agreement to be a deviation FROM.
RelatedEntity and RelatedEntityJoinField (Contract Template Modifications / ContractID) are
already columns on this same row and are deliberately NOT duplicated inside the blob — two
sources of truth where the JSON copy wins silently.
Keyed by entity NAMES, never the row's ID: EntityRelationship IDs are minted by CodeGen, so a
hardcoded UUID stops matching the first time this database is rebuilt from zero — routine here,
since pre-production schema changes edit the baseline in place.
Declares Contract Templates -> Contract Template Provisions as a related-record collection.
R-11 REMOVED the Sequence column and this collection's auto-numbering with it. Ordering is now
ProvisionSortKey ASC — a derived collation key computed from ProvisionNumber, which sorts
naturally ('1.9' before '1.10') where the number itself does not. The old maintained int was a
second copy of an order the number already stated, and the two had already disagreed in the seed.
Both writers go through it, which is the point: item 4's seed of the current Master Agreement's
clause list and item 7's registry UI where finance registers the NEXT version. One code path, so
the seed exercises what the UI will do.
OnRemove 'delete': a provision without its template version is not an orphan worth keeping. Note
this deletes the PROVISION row, and a modification pointing at it is blocked by its FK — which is
correct: you cannot retract a clause that a signed contract records a deviation from.
